note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Chest tightness with wheeze and cough for about 3 hours; accompanying mild shortness of breath.
- Onset/duration/progression: Acute onset 3 hours ago; symptoms persistent; night-time variation noted (worse at night).
- Context and triggers: Recent viral URIs/cold last week; ongoing cold symptoms (sore throat, runny nose). History of asthma; hay fever and dust allergy.
- Associated symptoms: Non-productive cough; slight shortness of breath on exertion (e.g., stairs); no chest pain reported.
- Prior episodes: Prior asthma exacerbations during adolescence; hospital admission with intubation in high school; otherwise relatively well-controlled with inhalers when used.
- Medications prior to visit: Ventolin (salbutamol) inhaler and Clenil Modulite inhaler; both ran out about a week ago and were not in use.
- Allergies: No drug allergies documented; dust sensitivity and milk protein allergy in childhood.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (history of severe exacerbation requiring intubation in adolescence)
- Eczema (history)
- Allergies: dust, milk protein (childhood)
- Hay fever/allergic rhinitis
- Family history: mother with eczema; father with asthma

Physical Examination:
- No objective vitals or exam findings documented.
- Patient reports wheeze, tight chest, and exertional dyspnea; able to walk on flat with mild SOB, no SOB at rest; no chest pain reported.

Impression:
- Acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by a recent viral URI/cold with wheeze and chest tightness.

Management Plan:
- Medications prescribed:
  - Inhaled therapy: Clenil Modulite (inhaled corticosteroid) and Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhalers; instructions to use Clenil in the morning and Ventolin PRN; spacer to improve lung delivery (spacer provided).
  - Oral corticosteroid: 5-day course; two tablets in the morning; note potential side effects discussed.
- Devices: Spacer prescribed with usage instructions.
- Activity/work: Self-certify for 7 days; rest as symptoms improve.
- Monitoring and safety: If Ventolin needed more than every 3 hours at any time, seek medical attention.
- Follow-up: Not explicitly specified; plan to have inhalers delivered within the hour.

Patient Summary:
- Daniel, a 26-year-old with asthma, presents with a 3-hour history of chest tightness, wheeze, and a non-productive cough after a recent cold. He lacks inhalers at the moment. Treatment plan includes restarted inhalers (Salbutamol and Clenil Modulite) with a spacer, plus a 5-day course of oral steroids, and short-term work absence. He was advised on when to seek urgent care and to rest until improved.

Key Takeaways:
- Use prescribed inhaler regimen (Clenil Modulite daily with PRN Ventolin) and utilize the spacer for better delivery.
- Start the 5-day oral steroid course; monitor for side effects as labeled.
- Seek medical attention if Ventolin use exceeds every 3 hours or if symptoms worsen (increased shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness).

Next Steps:
- Ensure timely delivery of inhalers and spacer.
- Return for follow-up or urgent care if symptoms escalate or fail to improve with treatment.
- Consider future follow-up to reassess asthma control and per inhaler-escalation plan.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO2), lung auscultation findings, peak flow measurement, smoking status, immunization status, and comprehensive meds reconciliation beyond patient-reported inhalers.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional interruptions but overall coherent; no inaudible sections affecting key clinical content.
